models_evaluated: Celsus Mammography (Faster R-CNN with ResNet-50 backbone; versions 0.14.0–0.17.0)

links.outcome: Calibration testing against predefined AUC and accuracy-deviation thresholds before clinical integration
links.effect: Initial model fell below the AUC threshold (0.81). After developer updates, version 0.15.0 reached AUC 0.81 and no metric deviated >10%, enabling PACS integration.
links.quote: Initial calibration testing of the AI model yielded promising results; however, the AUC and relative accuracy deviation fell below the established thresholds ( Figure 5 a, Table 6 ).

links.outcome: Monthly technical monitoring of missing or incomplete AI outputs
links.effect: Defects (no output or incomplete image analysis) exceeded the 10% threshold several times. The average defect proportion declined from 9.0% to 1.0% after feedback-driven fixes.
links.quote: The average proportion of technical defects declined from 9.0% to 1.0%, while the clinical assessment score improved from 63.4 to 72.0.

links.outcome: Monthly expert radiologist review of sampled AI outputs (clinical assessment score)
links.effect: Across 1160 sampled studies, the clinical assessment score improved from 63.4 to 72.0. A dip in months 15–16 followed a change of reviewer.
links.quote: The clinical evaluation plot shows a steady upward trend ( Figure 7 ).

Systematic relay of tester and radiologist feedback to the developer to drive iterative model updates

links.outcome: Detection and correction of functional defects before clinical integration
links.effect: Functional testing of version 0.14.0 identified two discrepancies: missing research-use labeling and color masks unsuitable for monochrome monitors. Both were resolved following developer changes and re-testing.
links.quote: After implementing the requested changes, re-testing we undertaken to make sure that both discrepancies had been resolved.

links.outcome: Local diagnostic performance against acceptance thresholds and claimed accuracy
links.effect: Initial AUC was 0.73, below the 0.81 acceptance threshold; relative accuracy deviation also failed acceptance criteria.
links.quote: Initial calibration testing of the AI model yielded promising results; however, the AUC and relative accuracy deviation fell below the established thresholds ( Figure 5 a, Table 6 ).

links.outcome: Technical failures associated with local configuration and examination parameters
links.effect: Technical defects exceeded the 10% threshold, predominantly involving incomplete image analysis; identified contributors included mammography unit configuration problems and incorrect examination parameters.
links.quote: Key contributing factors included mammography unit configuration problems, incorrect examination parameters set by technicians, PACS technical issues, and AI developer errors.

links.outcome: Technical defects and clinical assessment following monitoring-driven corrective updates
links.effect: Following iterative testing, monitoring, feedback, and updates, average technical defects declined from 9.0% to 1.0%; clinical assessment score improved from 63.4 to 72.0 in an uncontrolled before–after comparison.
links.quote: The average proportion of technical defects declined from 9.0% to 1.0%, while the clinical assessment score improved from 63.4 to 72.0.

links.outcome: Functional testing findings
links.effect: Initial expert radiologist review of AI outputs identified missing labels and inappropriate use of color graphic masks.
links.quote: Initial functional testing of the AI model (version 0.14.0) revealed two inconsistencies with the Baseline Functional Requirements: (1) absence of a “For research purposes only” label in both DICOM SR and additional image series, and (2) using color graphic masks to highlight pathological findings ( Figure 4 ).

links.outcome: Initial calibration testing performance
links.effect: Validation on local historical data found that the model's initial AUC and relative accuracy deviation failed to meet established thresholds.
links.quote: Initial calibration testing of the AI model yielded promising results; however, the AUC and relative accuracy deviation fell below the established thresholds ( Figure 5 a, Table 6 ).

links.outcome: Performance after model adjustments
links.effect: Following model adjustments based on local testing, the AUC improved by 24.7% (from 0.73 to 0.91) and accuracy by 15.6%.
links.quote: Specifically, the AUC rose by 24.7% (from 0.73 to 0.91), the accuracy improved by 15.6% (from 0.77 to 0.89), sensitivity grew by 37.1% (from 0.62 to 0.85), and specificity increased by 10.7% (from 0.84 to 0.93).

links.outcome: Performance of updated model version
links.effect: Repeat local calibration testing of the updated model version verified that the AUC increased to 0.81, meeting acceptance criteria.
links.quote: The second calibration testing of model version 0.15.0 demonstrated an improvement in diagnostic accuracy. The AUC increased to 0.81, meeting the threshold criteria, and no metric deviated downward by more than 10% compared to the claimed values ( Figure 5 b, Table 6 ).

links.outcome: Technical defects over time
links.effect: Technical monitoring detected instances where technical defects, such as incomplete image analysis or missing outputs, exceeded the 10% threshold.
links.quote: The technical defect monitoring plot highlights several instances where the technical defects exceeded the established threshold ( Figure 6 a).

screen.reason: Empirically evaluates a multi-stage lifecycle testing, prospective clinical monitoring, and radiologist feedback loop for deployment of a mammographic AI across 112 medical centers.

primary.practice: lifecycle-based testing, continuous clinical monitoring, and feedback-driven model updates
